speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing agitation and notice a yellowish tint to your skin and eyes; have you noticed any pain in your right upper abdomen or changes in your urine or stool color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis C infection (likely co-infected with Hepatitis A or B given high-risk sexual behavior) in a 20-year-old male, complicated by possible acute liver failure or sepsis from cocaine use.

I have made a diagnosis based on the clinical presentation of jaundice, agitation, and high-risk behaviors, but I will now request further testing to confirm the specific viral etiology and liver function status. REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Liver Function Tests (AST, ALT, Bilirubin, Alkaline Phosphatase), Hepatitis Serology Panel (A, B, C), and Complete Blood Count.
